newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary-Russia talks delay gas delivery to MOL.
newsitem.headline: Hungary-Russia talks delay gas delivery to MOL.

text.p: Delivery of 1.4 billion cubic metres of gas from Kazakhstan to Hungarian oil and gas company MOL Rt is being delayed by slow Hungarian-Russian inter-government talks, a Hungarian official said on Monday.
"Kazakhstan does not have a pipeline, but we need the gas," Istvan Tamas of Hungary's Industry and Trade Ministry told Reuters.
Kazakhstan last year signed an agreement saying it would ship 1.4 billion cubic metres of natural gas to Hungary in return for Hungarian development of the Yamburg gas field.
The shipment would have to come through Russia, which seems to have little interest in bringing talks to a successful ending, Tamas said.
"Kazakhstan is willing to honour its commitment...but the Russian side is more interested in selling its own gas (to Hungary)," he said.

MOL would have to pay a higher price for the Yamburg gas than for other deliveries from Russia, but MOL's half-year report said there was little chance for the trilateral deal to be sealed in the near future.
"These talks between the three countries have been going on for a year and we don't know the talks will be finished," Janos Szito, director of MOL's gas and oil trading business, told Reuters.
Tamas was also unable to tell when talks would come to a conclusion.

The deal would be important for MOL as it would reduce losses the company incurs due to the fact that it imports gas at or near world market prices while it sells the gas at state-controlled prices adjusted quarterly.
In the first half of 1997, MOL sold 6.5 billion cubic metres of gas, of which imports, mainly from Russia, accounted for 65 percent or 4.2 billion cubic metres.
Imported gas was then sold at an average loss of five forints per cubic metre or a total 4.6 billion forints for the first half of 1997.
